Infra & Chips.content: [![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/original/3d29ee764468946010cfa143e7c78b54:5d0164ae187a91ef56d93fd8ff9f0c71/ai-magazine-light-logo.png)](/ "Home") Article Infrastructure # The Unbelievable Attributes of NVIDIA's Global Strategy By[Adam Pond](/author/adam-pond) October 01, 2026 undefined mins Share this article **Prioritise Us** on Google Share this article **Prioritise Us** on Google ![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/2fe15005f4f6ddfecee9dc84b5b42aed:ce4068f9925973be3ebb58e8d5fd5930/gettyimages-2286326398.webp) Jensen Huang is the CEO at NVIDIA. Credit: Getty Images NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's unprecedented growth strategy has built the former startup focussed on GPUs for gaming into a supercompute infrastructure giant Few companies in history have changed shape as quickly as [NVIDIA](https://aimagazine.com/company/nvidia). A business once known for the graphics cards that powered video games is now the engine room of the global AI economy, and the most valuable listed company on Earth. On 25 September 2026, NVIDIA's market capitalisation reached US$5.4trn, ahead of Apple, Alphabet and [Microsoft](https://aimagazine.com/company/microsoft). Its latest quarter delivered US$96.2bn in revenue, more than double the figure a year earlier. Behind those numbers sits a strategy NVIDIA CEO [Jensen Huang](https://aimagazine.com/executive/jensen-huang) has refined for three decades: build the full stack, from silicon and networking to software and complete systems, then sell it as a factory rather than a chip. AI Magazine examines how that approach works, who NVIDIA builds with, who it sells to and where it goes next. > AI has reached its inflection point. It's doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue > > NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang The coming year and a half will test whether NVIDIA can turn record bookings into delivered gigawatts. Credit: NVIDIA ## From chipmaker to AI factory builder NVIDIA no longer sells components. It sells AI factories: complete systems that combine GPUs, CPUs, networking, memory and software into infrastructure that produces tokens, the units of AI output. The results show how well that message lands. In fiscal 2026 (February 2025 to January 2026), revenue hit a record US$215.9bn, up 65%, with data centre sales of US$193.7bn. In Q2 of fiscal 2027 (May to July 2026), data centre revenue reached US$89.0bn, up 117% year on year, while gross margin held at 75%. The product line has widened at the same pace. Blackwell led every category of MLPerf Training 6.0. Vera Rubin, the six-chip platform that succeeds it, is ramping to full production and Vera Rubin NVL72 topped its MLPerf Inference v6.1 debut. Around it sit the Vera CPU for agentic AI, the Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator, Spectrum-6 switches with co-packaged optics and BlueField-4 security. [At the edge](https://technologymagazine.com/news/nvidia-autonomous-tech-to-supercharge-chip-design), RTX Spark brings a one-petaflop superchip to Windows PCs, while Cosmos 3, Isaac GR00T and [Alpamayo 2 Super push NVIDIA into robots and robotaxis](https://evmagazine.com/news/autonomous-driving-physical-ai-what-is-nvidias-alpamayo). ![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/vLfrBembjsk/hqdefault.jpg) Jensen framed the shift in the company's August results statement: "AI has reached its inflection point. It's doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue." NVIDIA has stopped selling chips and started selling the factories that manufacture intelligence. “We’re going through a major platform shift," Jensen has previously told CNBC. Delivering those outcomes is harder and takes a significant amount of experience to be successful. Training a frontier model, fine-tuning an industry model, running high-volume inference and supporting agentic AI place different demands on infrastructure, processes and people. Implementing AI may include a single-purpose turnkey configuration that will accommodate one line of business, or the business may demand a more strategic approach to capitalize on the economies of scale and create AI as a multi-tenant service, designed to accommodate the multitude of mainstream business requirements. That is the value of an AI factory, bringing the complete AI lifecycle together so a cost-effective infrastructure can be designed around the mission, scaled with demand, secured as needed and operated as a dependable source of intelligence. The AI factory is designed to deliver the capacity, performance, utilization and business value customers expect. ## From AI workload to business outcome An AI factory is an integrated solution for data ingestion, model development, training, fine-tuning, inference, monitoring and continuous improvement. Its purpose is to turn data into intelligence repeatedly and efficiently—whether that intelligence supports a clinician, an engineer, a researcher, a public service or an enterprise application. Achieving that goal requires more than choosing an accelerated processor. Compute must match the business model and expected workloads. Networking and data pipelines must keep accelerators supplied. Storage must support the volume and velocity of data. Software must provision resources and orchestrate jobs. Security, governance and multi-tenancy must reflect who will use the environment and what data they can access. Infra & Chips.content: ![country_code](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/1x1-00000000.png) [Skip to content](#primary) # How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast Running on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and accelerated by continuous inference optimizations through OpenAI’s models, GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast delivers faster model responses across code generation, tool use and interactive applications. October 1, 2026 by [Dion Harris](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/dionharris/ "Posts by Dion Harris") [0 Comments](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/gpus-openai-gpt-6-astra-ultrafast/#disqus_thread) Share This Article * [X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fgpus-openai-gpt-6-astra-ultrafast%2F) * [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fgpus-openai-gpt-6-astra-ultrafast%2F) * [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fgpus-openai-gpt-6-astra-ultrafast%2F&title=How+NVIDIA+GPUs+Help+Accelerate+OpenAI%E2%80%99s+GPT-6+Astra+Ultrafast+%7C+NVIDIA+Blog) * [Copy link Link copied!](# "Copy link to clipboard") ![](https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/twitter-gif-2104993966043320759-v5-1280x720.png) GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast, running on [NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/blackwell-architecture/), is available now in the OpenAI API and to eligible ChatGPT Work and Codex users.  Accelerated by inference optimizations through OpenAI’s models that tap into the capabilities of the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, Ultrafast offers up to 8x faster token generation than the Astra Standard mode. For developers, faster generation can shorten coding agents’ edit-test-debug cycles, reduce the time spent generating responses between tool calls and make interactive applications feel more responsive.  A faster response matters most when it’s repeated across a workflow: an agent writes code, uses a tool, checks the result and decides what to do next. Ultrafast brings Astra’s capabilities into these time-sensitive loops. The AI world just got a serious speed upgrade. [OpenAI](https://openai.com) announced GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast is now running on [NVIDIA's](https://nvidia.com) cutting-edge Blackwell architecture, delivering token generation speeds that are 8x faster than the standard Astra mode. The model went live today through the OpenAI API and is rolling out to eligible ChatGPT Work and Codex enterprise customers. This isn't just another incremental improvement - it's a fundamental shift in what's possible with AI inference. The performance gains come from deep optimizations that tap directly into Blackwell's architectural advantages, suggesting [NVIDIA](https://nvidia.com) and [OpenAI](https://openai.com) have been working closely to squeeze every ounce of performance from the silicon. The timing is particularly interesting given the broader AI infrastructure arms race. While competitors like [Google](https://google.com) push their own TPU advantages and [Amazon](https://amazon.com/?tag=techbuzz0f-20) promotes Trainium chips, this [NVIDIA](https://nvidia.com)-[OpenAI](https://openai.com) partnership demonstrates how hardware-software co-optimization can deliver step-function improvements that pure scale alone can't match. Blackwell's architecture was specifically designed for transformer workloads, featuring enhanced memory bandwidth and specialized tensor processing units that align perfectly with large language model requirements. The 8x speedup suggests [OpenAI](https://openai.com) has rewritten core inference routines to take advantage of these architectural improvements rather than simply porting existing code. Advertisement Developers accessing the new model through the API will need to specify the Ultrafast variant, though [OpenAI](https://openai.com) hasn't disclosed pricing details yet. The company's typical approach suggests premium pricing for the enhanced performance, but the cost-per-token could still work out favorably given the dramatic speed improvements. This launch also signals [NVIDIA's](https://nvidia.com) continued dominance in AI training and inference, even as competitors work to chip away at their market position. The deep integration with [OpenAI's](https://openai.com) flagship model creates a compelling moat that will be difficult for alternatives to match without similar hardware-software partnerships.
